verses.text: After the uproar ended, Paul sent for the disciples, encouraged them, said goodbye, and left for Macedonia.
He traveled through those regions, giving the believers many words of encouragement, and then came to Greece.
He spent three months there. Just as he was about to sail for Syria, the Jews plotted against him, so he decided to return through Macedonia.
Sopater from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from Asia went with him.
They went ahead and waited for us in Troas.
After the Festival of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi and joined them in Troas five days later. We stayed there for seven days.
On the first day of the week, we gathered to break bread. Paul spoke to them and planned to leave the next day. He kept talking until midnight.
There were many lamps burning upstairs where we were gathered.
A young man named Eutychus was sitting in a window. As Paul kept speaking, Eutychus grew drowsier and fell into a deep sleep. He fell from the third floor and was picked up dead.
Paul went down, bent over him, and held him close. “Don’t panic,” he said. “He’s alive.”
Paul went back upstairs, broke bread and ate. He talked with them for a long time, until daybreak, and then left.
They took the young man home alive and were greatly comforted.
We went ahead to the ship and sailed for Assos, where we planned to pick up Paul. He had arranged to go there by land.
When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went to Mitylene.
The next day we sailed across from Chios. The day after that we reached Samos, stayed at Trogyllium, and the following day arrived in Miletus.
Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus so he wouldn’t lose time in Asia. He was hurrying to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.
From Miletus he sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church to meet him.
When they arrived, he said, “You know how I lived among you from the first day I came to Asia.
“I served the Lord with humility, with many tears, and through the troubles caused by the Jews’ plots against me.
“I never held back from telling you anything that would help you. I taught you in public and from house to house.
“I urged both Jews and Greeks to turn to God and trust in our Lord Jesus.
“Now I’m going to Jerusalem, compelled by the Spirit, though I don’t know what will happen to me there.
“I only know that in every city the Holy Spirit warns me that prison and suffering are waiting for me.
“But my life isn’t what I’m focused on. I want to finish my course with joy and complete the ministry the Lord Jesus gave me: to testify to the Good News of God’s grace.
“Now I know none of you, among whom I traveled announcing God’s Kingdom, will see me again.
“So I declare to you today that I’m not responsible for anyone’s blood,
“because I never held back from telling you everything God wants you to know.
“Watch out for yourselves and for the whole flock. The Holy Spirit made you its overseers. Shepherd the church of the Lord and God, which he bought with his own blood.
“I know that after I leave, savage wolves will come among you and won’t spare the flock.
“Even some of you will twist the truth to draw disciples after yourselves.
“So stay alert. Remember that for three years I kept warning each of you night and day, often with tears.
“Now I entrust you to God and to his message of grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are set apart for God.
“I never wanted anyone’s silver, gold, or clothing.
“You know that these hands provided for my needs and for the people with me.
“In everything I did, I showed you that by working hard we should help the weak. Remember the Lord Jesus’ words: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
After saying this, Paul knelt down and prayed with them all.
They all wept openly, hugged Paul, and kissed him goodbye.
They were especially sad because he had said they would never see him again. Then they walked with him to the ship.
